by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.intervention: Creatine, alone or with an antidepressant

decisions.reason: Pooled randomised trials of creatine versus placebo in people with or without depression, with depressive symptoms as the outcome; all four parts match.

question.population: Adults, healthy or with an illness

decisions.reason: Looks at psychiatric symptoms of depression and bipolar disorder, mostly with creatine added to other treatment, not at memory or thinking.
Pools RCTs of creatine vs control in healthy and ill adults, with meta-analysed memory, attention and processing speed outcomes.
Pools RCTs of creatine vs placebo on memory in healthy people, with a separate older-adult subgroup that matches.
Reviews RCTs of oral creatine on memory and thinking in healthy people, including adults, though without a meta-analysis.
This is a commentary on a review with no abstract, not a systematic review that pooled trials itself.
This is a letter criticising the statistics of a creatine memory meta-analysis, not a systematic review itself.
This is an author's reply to a letter, with no abstract, not a systematic review that pooled trials.
Creatine vs placebo for cognition is covered, but only in healthy adults, among many supplements, and with no clear pooled analysis.

question.outcome: Body weight, body water or body fat

decisions.reason: Compares creatine plus β-alanine against either supplement alone, not against placebo, so it asks about the combination rather than creatine itself.
Meta-analysis of RCTs of creatine supplementation pooling body mass, fat-free mass and body fat percentage.
Pools RCTs of creatine versus placebo on body composition, but only in swimmers, a narrower group than healthy adults.
Placebo-controlled RCTs in healthy subjects on body composition, but only alternative creatine forms, not monohydrate, and results not clearly pooled.
Meta-analysis of randomised placebo-controlled creatine studies in humans, calculating effect sizes for body mass and lean body mass.
Creatine vs placebo with body weight and fat outcomes, but the participants are cancer patients or survivors, not healthy adults, and results were not pooled.
Pooled trials of creatine vs placebo on fat mass, but only in adults aged 50 or over, and creatine was always given alongside resistance training.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in trained athletes that includes creatine and reports endurance performance as an outcome.
Creatine vs placebo RCTs in adult athletes, but the endurance outcomes reported are muscular endurance and repeated sprints, not aerobic endurance.
Pooled placebo-controlled trials of creatine monohydrate on endurance performance in a trained population, which matches every part of the question.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in training athletes that compares creatine with placebo and includes endurance performance as an outcome.
Pooled placebo-controlled RCTs with an RT subgroup and lean mass and strength outcomes, but only in postmenopausal women (mean age about 62).
Pooled RCTs in adults aged 60+ comparing creatine plus RT with RT alone or placebo plus RT, measuring muscle strength and muscle mass.
Network meta-analysis in trained athletes comparing protein, creatine and omega-3; not about older adults.
Pooled trials in young men aged 18-30, not older adults.
Creatine plus RT vs placebo with an older-adult subgroup, but outcomes are strength and power only, with no lean mass.
Network meta-analysis of several supplements in athletes, not older adults.
Compares creatine plus beta-alanine with either supplement alone, not with placebo, and not in older adults.
Reviews polyphenol supplements for recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage, not creatine.
Creatine plus RT, but compares novice and experienced lifters and has no older-adult analysis.
Pools creatine trials in general populations for body composition, with no older-adult analysis.
Creatine vs placebo in older adults and people with chronic disease, measuring strength and lean mass, but not restricted to RT.
Creatine trials in swimmers, not older adults doing resistance training.
Creatine plus RT vs placebo plus RT with an age moderator, but measures only regional hypertrophy, not strength.
Looks at recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage, not long-term strength or lean mass in older adults.
Looks at markers of exercise-induced muscle damage in adults aged 20-60, not training adaptations in older adults.
Pooled RCTs of creatine plus RT vs placebo on strength and muscle mass, but only in older women.
Reviews alternative forms of creatine in healthy subjects, with no older-adult focus.
RCTs of creatine plus exercise vs exercise alone in older adults, but a narrative review with no pooling, and exercise is not only RT.
Reviews vitamins C and E after a single bout of exercise, not creatine.
Pools creatine vs placebo for upper-limb strength across all populations, with no older-adult analysis.
Training and an age subgroup match, but creatine is given together with protein in multi-ingredient supplements rather than alone.
Pools creatine vs placebo trials, but in all ages without an older-adult analysis, training isn't required, and only lower-limb strength is reported.
Pools placebo-controlled trials of creatine plus resistance training in older adults, with fat-free mass and strength outcomes.
Covers creatine trials in people aged 60+, but training isn't required, creatine is mixed with other supplements, and results aren't pooled.
Creatine for treating hereditary muscle disease in people of all ages, without resistance training: a different question.
Pools creatine vs placebo strength trials, but in healthy adults who were mostly young men, with no separate older-adult analysis.
Pools creatine vs placebo trials on lean mass and performance, but not in older adults and without requiring resistance training.
Creatine vs control on strength in a general population with only a middle-aged/elderly subgroup; lean mass not pooled and training not limited to resistance.
Older adults, creatine plus exercise vs placebo plus exercise with 1RM strength, but training is general exercise and lean mass is not reported.
Creatine plus resistance training vs placebo on strength, but limited to adults under 50.
RCTs in older adults pooling creatine plus resistance training vs placebo plus resistance training on strength and lean tissue mass.
Pools many nutritional supplements in sarcopenia patients with no separate creatine plus resistance training analysis.
Cancer patients, no resistance training specified, body composition only, and narrative review without pooling.
Young people during limb immobilisation and rehabilitation, not older adults doing resistance training.
Young adults, with muscle damage markers after exercise as outcomes rather than strength or lean mass.
Older adults, creatine vs placebo during resistance training, pooled lean tissue mass and strength outcomes.
Adults 50+, creatine vs placebo during resistance training, but the outcome is fat mass rather than strength or lean mass.
RCTs in adults over 50 with creatine plus resistance training vs training alone, but the outcome is bone mineral density.
RCTs in older adults, creatine vs placebo during resistance training, pooled lean tissue mass and chest and leg press strength.

question.outcome: Strength or repeated short, hard exercise

decisions.reason: Network meta-analysis of RCTs in healthy active people includes creatine versus placebo for jump and relative peak power.
Creatine versus placebo with strength outcomes, but the population is postmenopausal women with a mean age of about 62, not adults under 50.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in trained athletes reports creatine effects on muscle strength.
RCTs in healthy adult athletes pooled creatine versus placebo for sprint, jump and repeated-sprint ability.
Creatine is pooled with protein and amino acids, always given with exercise, and the women include menopausal stages; there is no separate creatine analysis.
Creatine for patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain, so it treats illness rather than healthy adults, and the trials are not pooled.
Pooled RCTs of creatine in healthy men aged 18-30 for strength, Wingate power and jump.
Pooled RCTs of creatine versus placebo on strength and power in adults, with a younger-adult subgroup.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in soccer players includes creatine versus placebo for jump height.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in volleyball athletes includes creatine versus placebo for vertical jump.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in athletes includes creatine versus placebo for jump and sprint performance.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs in combat athletes includes creatine versus placebo for mean and peak power.
The comparison is creatine plus beta-alanine versus either supplement alone, not versus placebo, and results are not pooled.
Reviews polyphenol supplements, not creatine.
Acute creatine is pooled with caffeine and carbohydrate rinse alongside a conditioning activity; there is no clear creatine-versus-placebo analysis.
COPD patients receiving coenzyme Q10 plus creatine, with lung function and endurance outcomes.
Creatine versus placebo in active females on strength and anaerobic outcomes, but the trials are summarised narratively, not pooled.
Pooled RCTs of creatine versus placebo in swimmers for single sprint and repeated interval performance.
Pooled double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of creatine in adults aged 18-60 for repeated sprint ability.
Creatine versus placebo after muscle-damaging exercise, but the pooled outcomes are mainly blood markers (CK, LDH).
Creatine vs a non-creatine comparator in adult RCTs, but the outcome is strength recovery after muscle damage, and ages run up to 60.
Placebo-controlled RCTs in healthy people, but it covers only alternative creatine forms, not monohydrate, and pools no results.
Creatine vs placebo RCTs with pooled strength, sprint and anaerobic outcomes, but only in soccer players, a narrower group.
Creatine plus exercise vs exercise alone for strength, but in older adults rather than adults under 50.
Creatine with strength and Wingate outcomes, but only in vegetarians, a narrower group, and it includes non-randomised studies.
The intervention is vitamins C and E, not creatine.
Pooled RCTs of creatine vs placebo on upper-limb strength in short exercise, across population groups.
Strength outcomes in RCTs, but creatine is only given together with protein in multi-ingredient supplements.
Pooled RCTs of creatine vs placebo on lower-limb strength in exercises under 3 minutes.
The outcomes are heat tolerance and hydration, not strength or repeated short, hard exercise.
Adults over 65 given a range of supplements with exercise; creatine is one of several, so both population and intervention differ.
Pooled placebo-controlled trials of creatine on maximal strength and power in healthy adults.
Pooled randomised placebo-controlled trials of creatine on short, high-intensity and repeated-bout exercise performance.
Pooled creatine vs control on muscle strength, with a subgroup comparing young and middle-aged/elderly people, so a younger-adult analysis is included.
Population is swimmers only, and the creatine result reported is for creatine combined with sodium bicarbonate, not creatine alone.
Pooled creatine plus resistance training vs placebo on upper- and lower-body strength in adults under 50.
Outcome is endurance performance, not strength or repeated short, hard exercise.
RCTs of creatine vs placebo on peak and mean anaerobic power, but only in athletes, a narrower group than healthy adults.
Placebo-controlled trials in young people, but during limb immobilisation and rehab; results were not pooled.
Pooled RCTs of creatine vs placebo across all ages on 'metabolic performance', with no separate analysis for under-50s or for strength.
Outcome is cognitive performance, not strength or exercise.

question.outcome: Kidney function, or blood creatinine and eGFR

decisions.reason: Meta-analysis of creatine versus control on serum creatinine and GFR; the abstract doesn't say whether the studies were randomised or who the participants were.
Pools placebo-controlled RCTs on creatinine and GFR, but mixes healthy people with CKD and hemodialysis patients and reports no healthy-only analysis.
Pools RCTs of creatine on serum creatinine, urea and eGFR, with subgroups by participants' physical status.
Covers creatine and kidney safety, but only in adolescents, includes cohort studies and reports no pooled analysis.
